about: A rewrite of the grep search tool in Rust, aiming to work the same as GNU grep.

prs.title: The last matching include or exclude rule now decides
prs.broken: When a search mixed rules for which files to include and which to skip, any skip rule won, whatever the order. GNU grep lets the last rule that matches a file decide, so the two picked different files.
prs.changed: The rules are now kept in the order you typed them, and the last one that matches a file decides, like GNU grep.
prs.matters: Searches over a folder look at the same files as GNU grep.

prs.title: A stray closing bracket in a search pattern is now plain text
prs.broken: GNU grep treats a closing round bracket with no opening one as an ordinary character. This grep rejected the pattern with an error and stopped.
prs.changed: Extended patterns now accept it as a literal character, while basic patterns keep their existing rules.
prs.matters: Scripts that search with these patterns work the same as with GNU grep.

prs.title: Line numbers and byte offsets now line up like GNU grep
prs.broken: With the option that lines up output with a tab, a file read from standard input got far too much padding, and byte offsets got none at all.
prs.changed: The padding now follows the size of the input and also covers byte offsets, matching GNU grep.
prs.matters: Output has the same columns as GNU grep, so scripts that read it keep working.
